objective: Implement deterministic frontloaded planning for the governed control plane.

intent_contract.objective: Implement deterministic frontloaded planning for the governed control plane.
success_criteria: Intent, readiness, compiler, gap, coverage, and sufficiency artifacts are emitted deterministically.
The plan compiles deterministically into execution-plan.v1 without semantic drift.
non_goals: Do not build a separate planning-only runtime.
authority_sensitive_decisions: Global control-plane policy wording and escalation semantics.

ambiguity_classification.statement: How much frontloaded structure is required before execution approval.

constraints: Align planning outputs directly to the v2.7 autonomous-completion contract and packet DAG.
implementation_plan: Extend the plan contract and schema for sufficiency and frontloaded planning fields.
Add compile and verify scripts for pre-approval artifacts.
Update validators, fixtures, and runtime docs to enforce the new frontloaded path.

solution_ladder.L1_patch: Patch only the immediate validator or workflow that exposed the gap.
solution_ladder.L2_abstraction: Extend the planning contract, validator, and review policy as a reusable abstraction for future planning work.
solution_ladder.L3_operating_surface: Create a full operator surface that standardizes layer choice across all planning and execution interfaces.

layer_justification: The issue recurs across non-trivial planning work, but the bounded fix is to harden the shared planning contract and review path rather than create a broader operating surface immediately.
why_not_lower: A local patch would leave the same low-layer planning instinct to recur in future governed tasks.
why_not_higher: A dedicated operating surface would be broader than needed for this contract-focused change and would add speculative framework work now.
existing_primitives_considered: planning-gate validate_plan.py already gates non-trivial work
route_manifest.json already owns runtime route defaults
CLAUDE.md already owns global operator policy
reuse_first_decision: Harden the existing route manifest and planning-gate validators instead of creating a new control-plane subsystem.
budget_exception_justification: This pass deliberately hardens shared policy, schemas, validators, and tests across the control plane; a smaller change would not enforce anti-overengineering fail-closed behavior.
new_surface_proof: No new runtime surface is introduced. The change only constrains existing planning-gate and route-manifest primitives.
swarm_justification: This fixture intentionally exercises the bounded-swarm validation path so scheduler and convergence checks remain covered by tests.

definition_of_done.criterion: Frontloaded planning artifacts and runtime compatibility checks validate deterministically.
Automated tests cover compile, verify, and plan-validation failure modes.
Out-of-policy contracts and unstable IDs are blocked by deterministic validators.
Compiler, gap, coverage, and sufficiency artifacts are emitted as machine-readable JSON.
definition_of_done.verification: Inspect plan.compiler.json, plan.gaps.json, plan.coverage.json, and plan.sufficiency.json under planning_artifacts.

definition_of_done.criterion: Revision and blocked paths preserve explicit unresolved-gap output without silent approval.

definition_of_done.verifier_acceptance_condition: Sufficiency artifact marks the plan approved and runtime-compatible.

defined_terms.authoritative: Planning-gate validators and committed planning artifacts are the source of truth over operator prose.
defined_terms.valid: Only exact Phase-1 contract shapes and enumerated values are accepted.
defined_terms.same_host: The same canonical control-plane host identity for local process ownership checks.
defined_terms.occupied_slot: A bounded surface that is already claimed by the current plan contract and may not be reused implicitly.
defined_terms.belongs_to_repo: An artifact resolves back to the expected canonical workspace or artifacts root.
defined_terms.no_mutation: The action returns an explicit error and does not change governed runtime state.

authority_boundary.source_of_truth: The plan payload plus planning-gate validator contract are authoritative.
authority_boundary.rewrite_precedence: Validator recomputation wins over stale operator review text or cached assumptions.
continuity_rules: Stable packet ids and requirement ids must be preserved.
Execution-ready status cannot be inferred when contract validation fails.

repair_boundary.allowed_repair_path: Only the compile/verify/validate planning-gate flow may repair planning artifacts.
mutators_forbidden_repair: compile_plan.py must not silently widen scope
validate_plan.py must not invent missing fields

mutator_contracts.not_applicable_reason: This fixture exercises contract validation for scripts and artifacts, not a public mutating API surface.

read_contracts.not_applicable_reason: This fixture does not define a public read API surface.

overengineering_guardrails.minimum_value_loop: author plan -> compile intent -> compile plan -> verify plan -> validate plan

reuse_proof.why_not_lower: A narrower patch would not keep future plans from drifting back into implicit contracts.
reuse_proof.why_not_higher: A broader operator surface would add control-plane scope before it is needed.
